# Signal Weekly — Nov 2–Nov 9, 2026

*Nov 2–Nov 9, 2026*

This week’s tech digest brings fresh updates from space sims to AI‑powered music, plus handy hardware tips for your everyday workflow.

## Tech news

- **[EVE Online's new expansion looks to make it simpler than ever to get into a huge space battle: 'Every 10 weeks or so, you're gonna know: I can roll up with whatever I have and go shoot some structures and have a big fight'](https://www.pcgamer.com/games/mmo/eve-onlines-new-expansion-looks-to-make-it-simpler-than-ever-to-get-into-a-huge-space-battle-every-10-weeks-or-so-youre-gonna-know-i-can-roll-up-with-whatever-i-have-and-go-shoot-some-structures-and-have-a-big-fight/)** (PC Gamer) — EVE Online lowers entry barriers, inviting casual players into massive battles every few weeks.
- **[Authors Can Defend Against AI Allegations With ‘Paper Trail’ Tools. Is It Enough?](https://www.wired.com/story/authors-can-defend-against-ai-allegations-with-paper-trail-tools/)** (Wired) — Authors now have a ‘paper trail’ tool to protect their IP in the AI‑driven content era.
- **[Synaptics sends cease-and-desist order to creator of open-source DisplayLink driver, dares him to publicize its threats](https://www.tomshardware.com/peripherals/docking-stations-hubs/synaptics-sends-cease-and-desist-order-to-creator-of-open-source-displaylink-driver-dares-him-to-publicize-its-threats-dev-reverse-engineers-displaylink-using-claude-ai-and-rust-synaptics-threatens-to-bill-creator-for-legal-documentation)** (Tom's Hardware) — Proprietary tech clashes with open‑source innovation, impacting Linux developers.
- **[CHAPEA Mission 2 Crew Reflects After 378 Days on Simulated Mars](https://www.nasa.gov/centers-and-facilities/johnson/chapea-mission-2-crew-reflects-after-378-days-on-simulated-mars/)** (NASA) — NASA crew insights from 378 days on simulated Mars inform future Mars mission design.
- **[These Robotic Arms Are Powered by Algae. Watch How They Move](https://www.wired.com/story/these-robotic-arms-are-made-of-algae-watch-how-they-move/)** (Wired) — Algae‑powered robotic arms showcase a green energy source for robotics.

## Reviews

- **[How to use your laptop as a second monitor](https://www.engadget.com/2309277/how-to-use-laptop-second-desktop-monitor/)** (Engadget) — Turn your laptop into a second monitor—expand workspace without extra gear.
- **[Why your USB device isn't showing up on your MacBook and how you can fix it](https://www.engadget.com/2309279/why-usb-device-not-showing-up-macbook-fixes/)** (Engadget) — Quick USB fixes keep your MacBook workflow smooth and hassle‑free.

---

Stay curious, stay tech‑savvy, and enjoy the week’s highlights!
thread: 🚀 EVE Online’s new expansion makes huge space battles accessible to casual players—every 10 weeks you can jump in and fight!
📝 Authors now have a ‘paper trail’ tool to defend against AI‑generated plagiarism claims—protect your IP!
🤖 Synaptics’ cease‑and‑desist against an open‑source DisplayLink driver shows the clash between proprietary tech and Linux freedom.
🌌 NASA’s CHAPEA crew reflect on 378 days in a Mars simulation—valuable lessons for future crew psychology and design.
🌱 Algae‑powered robotic arms move with surprising grace—green energy meets robotics innovation.
💻 Turn your laptop into a second monitor—expand your workspace without buying new hardware.
